reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify baseline patterns in shared features with external XAI tools to quantify feature attributions, ensuring both structural and model-level insight into spurious correlations. This approach increases the reliability of detecting features that are common across misclassified instances and have high predictive influence despite lacking semantic relevance.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify all features that are present in both instance 13590 and instance 44018 and check for any other misclassified instances that share these features.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across the two instances and potential commonality with other misclassified instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any of the shared features (e.g., occupation=Craft-repair, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse) have plausible spurious correlations with the target class (>50K) based on domain knowledge or data semantics.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justification for why a shared feature may be spurious and not semantically related to income prediction

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides a game-theoretic attribution score that captures individual feature importance across all instances, enabling detection of high-impact spurious features. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local and global interpretability, respectively, to validate the robustness of feature attributions. Sensitivity analysis confirms feature influence through ablation, helping isolate features that drive misclassification despite lack of semantic relevance.
